The "Wishonia" model represents a hypothetical equilibrium achieved through the systematic application of the strategies outlined in this text.

Previous chapters discussed the economic incentives for preventing mortality. This section illustrates the societal outcome of successful implementation.

The Wishonia model describes a civilization that eliminated warfare 4,297 years ago. This did not occur due to moral evolution. Rather, the society calculated that deceased citizens do not pay taxes, invent technologies, or produce offspring who subsequently pay taxes.

This chapter outlines the potential future state of Earth following the execution of these instructions. It serves as a projection of the trajectory humanity currently navigates.

## How the Model Works

Under the Wishonia framework, society does not feature:

- Wars (economically inviable)
- Disease (eradicated over approximately 50 Earth years)
- Death from old age (now optional; most residents opt out)
- Physical currency (proven inefficient)
- Committees deciding healthcare allocation (also inefficient)

The society does feature:

- AI-optimized resource allocation (maximizing marginal median happiness through wishocracy)
- Treatments tested on the entire population simultaneously
- Life expectancy defined by "boredom"
- An economy that rewards not killing people

Humanity possesses the capacity to construct this. Humans share the same atomic structure and neurological functions as the Wishonian model. The primary distinction is that the model society ceased spending resources on explosion technology during the equivalent of Earth's Stone Age.

## Projecting Earth's Transformation

### 2026: Year One - Implementation

Advocates convince enough humans to indicate agreement on the [global referendum](../strategy/global-referendum-academic.qmd). Securing 500 million signatures requires six months, which is faster than the historical adoption of hand-washing for disease prevention.

A [1% treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty-academic.qmd) passes.

Military contractors initially complain until presented with the [VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds](../economics/victory-bonds-academic.qmd) projections. With {{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} annual returns, resistance ceases. Lockheed Martin announces diversification into healthcare technology. This equates to a realization that preventing death is more profitable than causing it.

Even Congress understands {{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} returns. Money is the only language spoken fluently in that environment.

### 2028: The 2% Discovery

The population discovers something fascinating: not dying is pleasant.

After observing what {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}} could achieve, specifically [15 new treatments in the first year](../references.qmd#recovery-trial-100-days-to-cure), the demand increases. The 2% Treaty passes rapidly.

By 2028, spending reaches $54 billion annually on [a decentralized institutes of health](../solution/dih-academic.qmd).

Results:

- Cancer survival rates jump 20% in 24 months
- Five new diabetes treatments emerge that function effectively
- Depression treatments improve dramatically (reduced anxiety regarding nuclear war helps)

This marks the moment humans begin realizing they have been misaligned for a very long time.

### 2030: The Three Supers Begin

By 2030, humanity constructs an AI capable of executing 260 years of scientific progress per calendar year. This results from directing intelligent machines toward healing rather than missile targeting systems.

The AI receives one instruction: "maximize median health and happiness."

Its first suggestion: abolish the IRS. This is enacted. Nobody complains.
Second suggestion: universal basic income. This is enacted. Still no complaints.

Humans realize the AI is smarter than the aggregate of all historical economists. This is not difficult.

The Three Supers begin:

**Super-Wellbeing:** Depression is cured. Not "managed." Cured. Five different treatments exist. Side effects include uncontrollable happiness and 400% productivity increases because people stop wanting to die.

**Super-Longevity:** Aging is reversed in mice. The subjects are effectively negative-three years old. Human trials begin. Volunteers include everyone over 30 who owns a mirror.

**Super-Intelligence:** The AI begins solving problems. Human scientists were using crayons by comparison. The AI provides supercomputers.

Countries begin competing to redirect MORE military spending. It is the first arms race where everyone wins.

### 2035: The 5% Treaty - National Competition

Germany commits 5%.

Japan commits 6%.

Switzerland commits 100% and abolishes its military.

Observers note Switzerland barely possessed one.

Switzerland confirms this assessment.

The results:

- **Heart disease:** Monthly injection. Problem solved.
- **Alzheimer's:** AI identifies the pattern in 30 seconds. Humans missed it for 50 years.
- **Aging:** Slowed by 40%

- **Work week:** 20 hours. AI performs boring tasks. Humans perform interesting ones.

Average lifespan hits 95 years. Not just living longer. Living better.

A 90-year-old grandmother is not in a nursing home. She runs marathons and starts a third career.

In the Wishonia model, this is classified as "normal."

Current body patches include:

## A Typical Daily Routine in 2050

The following represents a typical Tuesday when the Three Supers are normalized:

**6:00 AM:** Wake up naturally. Body OS 12.3 optimizes sleep. The individual feels excellent. No alarm is needed because circadian rhythms are regulated perfectly.

**7:00 AM:** Breakfast. Outcome Labels indicate exactly how each food affects the body. Dark chocolate improves cognitive function by 23%. IQ is adjusted to 80 for morning news, then 200 for work. Science is adjustable now.

**9:00 AM:** Work on a passion project. Example: teaching dolphins to code. They outperform most bootcamp graduates. Universal Basic Income (funded by the peace dividend) means work is voluntary, not survival-based. Wishocracy allocation takes 3 seconds: 90% to curing blindness, 10% to curing baldness. An AI twin handles 10,000 other decisions while the human drinks coffee.

**12:00 PM:** Lunch with a friend who died in 2030. They got better. Death is reversible now. A great-great-grandmother (150, looks 25) joins via hologram from a Mars artist residency. Pets are technically minor deities. Nobody questions it.

**2:00 PM:** Learn Mandarin via neural download. Takes 4 minutes. Spanish, French, and Klingon were acquired yesterday. The AI reminds the human about a 3 PM meeting. It is missed. Nobody cares. The project finished itself using swarm intelligence.

**4:00 PM:** Annual health checkup. Nanobots scanned the body during sleep. They found and eliminated a precancerous cell at 3 cells, not 3 billion. An AI ran a billion simulations on the genome for recreation. Gut bacteria were optimized to increase intelligence by 15%. Cost: $0 (peace dividend covers it).

**6:00 PM:** Family dinner. Everyone is present because nobody dies anymore (unless they want to, which is their business). Planning next week's body modifications: a daughter wants wings, a son wants gills, the parent considers photosynthesis.

**9:00 PM:** Upload the day's experiences to collective consciousness. Download everyone else's. The individual has now lived 8 billion days in one day. Time is strange. Social media is tolerable because everyone is right about everything simultaneously.

**10:00 PM:** Sleep in a programmable dream suite. Tonight's dreams are designed by Pixar, sponsored by nobody. Sleep is a solved problem. The body repairs itself, reverses aging, and backs up consciousness. Tomorrow one might try being 25 again. Or a dolphin. Options are good.

## The Peace Dividend Economy

Even in paradise, economics matters. Money still exists. It simply flows differently.

As the 1% Treaty Fund's budget grew from {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}} to over a trillion, economic gravity shifted. Scientists and investors saw better returns curing Alzheimer's than building fighter jets. Peace became profitable. This marks the first time in history.

### Annual Global Redirected Funds (2050)

- From military budgets: $1.35 trillion
- Economic growth from healthy population: $3.5 trillion
- Reduced healthcare costs: $2.8 trillion
- Productivity gains from longevity: $4.1 trillion
- **Total Annual Peace Dividend: $11.75 trillion**

This follows the logic from [the Economic Case chapter](../economics/economics-academic.qmd) - $1.2T from the initial 1% treaty, scaled to 50% redirection over 25 years. Same principles. Bigger numbers.

That equates to $1,450 per human per year in actual new wealth. Not redistribution. New wealth generated by the absence of sickness and death.

## New Areas of Competition

Humans remain competitive. Competition simply shifts to better objectives:

**Health Olympics:** Countries compete for highest life expectancy. Japan and Switzerland tie at 112 years. The US attempts to catch up by banning corn syrup.

**Innovation Race:** Who cures diseases fastest? India announces spinal tissue regeneration. Brazil counters with hearing loss reversal. China grows new teeth. Wisdom teeth are available for re-installation if desired. Nobody knows why one would want them.

**Space Race 2.0:** Hotels, not missiles. Hilton Mars receives its fifth star. The Lunar golf course has a three-year waiting list.

**Happiness Wars:** Cities compete for highest quality of life. Copenhagen held the title for five years until Auckland installed mood-boosting streetlights. Detroit makes a comeback with free childcare and elder care.

## Corporate Transformation

The same companies that produced weapons now produce life:

**Lockheed Martin Health:** Cancer-detecting satellites spot tumors from orbit. Stock price: $12,000/share. Shareholders are satisfied.

**Raytheon Wellness:** Missile guidance systems make excellent surgical robots. 50 million perfect surgeries performed.

**Boston Dynamics:** Robots help elderly individuals walk. The dancing remains cute, but is now therapeutic.

**Palantir Health Insights:** Data analysis predicts disease outbreaks before they happen. Privacy-protected, transparent, saving lives.

## New Challenges

Challenges remain. They are simply better challenges:

**Longevity Overflow:** Too many healthy 100-year-olds want to work. More jobs are needed. Solution: three-day work weeks and multiple careers per lifetime.

**Education Inflation:** When living to 150, more education is required. Universities offer "Century Degrees": 100-year educational plans.

**Experience FOMO:** With health and time, people worry about missing experiences. Travel agencies book trips 50 years in advance.

**Purpose Anxiety:** When not worried about dying, people worry about meaning. Philosophy becomes the fastest-growing major.

These are luxury problems. Societies prefer them over cancer.

## The Treaties Keep Improving

The plan's genius was incremental design, detailed in [a 1% treaty chapter](../solution/1-percent-treaty-academic.qmd#the-ratchet-effect-how-to-boil-a-frog-the-frog-is-the-war-machine). Every few years, another referendum nudged the percentage up. Each increase funded more cures, created more value for bondholders, and built bigger coalitions demanding the next increase.

The ratchet clicked forward: 1% in 2026, then 2%, 3%, 5%, 10%, 25%, until 50% by 2050. $1.35 trillion annually redirected from weapons to cures.

### Why The Expansion Never Stopped

On Earth, they are called [Incentive Alignment Bonds](../solution/incentive-alignment-bonds-academic.qmd). In the Wishonia model, they are simply "obvious."

Here is what humans failed to realize when designing the system: the 10% allocation to political incentives was not just for passing the first treaty. It was the **scaling engine** that made every subsequent expansion inevitable.

| Year | Treaty | Political Incentive Pool | What Politicians Saw |
|:-----|:-------|:------------------------|:--------------------|
| 2026 | 1% | $2.7B/year | "Support this and career prospects improve" |
| 2028 | 2% | $5.4B/year | "Push for more and rewards double" |
| 2035 | 5% | $13.5B/year | "Military lobby can no longer compete" |
| 2040 | 10% | $27B/year | "Health spending is now the most rewarded position" |
| 2050 | 50% | $135B/year | "War is economically obsolete" |

The VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bond investors received their {{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} returns and were happy at 1%. But the politicians? Every expansion meant more rewards. They competed to expand faster.

By 2035, "support health spending" had become the single most rewarded political position on Earth. Military contractors pivoted not because of moral revelations, but because the politicians they usually lobbied now cared more about their IAB scores than campaign contributions.

Humans thought they were building a health funding mechanism. They actually built a political transformation engine. The 10% political allocation eventually became $135 billion annually, more than all previous global lobbying combined. At that point, war was not just unpopular. It was economically impossible.

Military spending is now mostly space military against asteroids and alien invasion preparedness. If aliens arrive, humanity wants to look healthy and prosperous, not armed and paranoid.

## 2050: The Three Supers Complete

**Super-Intelligence:** Complete. Every human accesses all knowledge instantly. Debates end in nanoseconds. Everyone is right about everything because all perspectives can be simulated simultaneously. Social media becomes tolerable.

**Super-Longevity:** Solved. Death is like moving to Ohio, technically possible but nobody does it. Some choose to die for artistic reasons. They get better. Death sues for wrongful termination.

**Super-Wellbeing:** Perfected. Suffering exists only in history classes. Students do not believe it was real. "People felt bad without choosing to? That is irrational."

The last military on Earth (North Korea, obviously) finally disbands. They were defending against an enemy that ceased existing in 2040. The soldiers become interpretive dancers. They are skilled.

Earth's status: Chose healing. Became magic. Next goal: befriend entropy.

## The Personal Future

Here is what life looks like in 2050:

**Health:** Live to 150+ (or forever). The body is programmable software, debug it, upgrade it, back it up. Death is optional. Most try it once for the experience.

**Wealth:** The peace dividend provides $50,000/year universal basic income. Money barely matters in post-scarcity. Work is play. Play is work. Both are optional.

**Family:** Humans meet their great-great-great-grandchildren. Family reunions happen in virtual dimensions because stadiums are too small. Pets are immortal and possibly telepathic.

**Purpose:** With survival handled, focus shifts to what matters: creating universes, solving entropy, communicating with extraterrestrials, becoming one with the cosmos, or perfecting the perfect sandwich. All valid.

**Death:** Like graduation, optional, reversible, mostly ceremonial. Some collect deaths like stamps. "I've died 47 times! Tokyo 2043 was my favorite."

## What Fixing Health Fixed

Nobody predicted this: fixing health fixed everything else.

**Climate Change:** Healthy people make long-term decisions. Solved by 2040 once everyone realized they would be alive to see the consequences.

**Poverty:** Healthy people are productive. Global GDP tripled when society stopped losing productive years to preventable disease.

**Education:** When life extends to 150, 20 years of education makes sense. Global literacy hit 99.9%.

**Innovation:** Healthy brains think better. More breakthrough discoveries occurred in 20 years than in the previous 200.

**Peace:** It is difficult to go to war when citizens live too long to throw away. Also, collaboration on curing remaining diseases takes priority.

**Happiness:** Not dying of preventable diseases makes people happier. Surprising, admittedly.

## Reality Check

Is everything perfect? No. Humans are still humans.

Society still has:

- Heartbreak (better therapies for healing)
- Disagreements (less deadly ones)
- Accidents (better emergency response)
- Natural disasters (better preparation and recovery)
- Existential questions (more time to ponder them)

The difference: these are problems of a thriving species, not a dying one.

Society stands at a bifurcation point.

Path A: [The Dystopia](moronia-academic.qmd) - Trillions spent on death. Society receives exactly what it paid for. Everyone dies.

Path B: Wishonia - 1% spent on life. Nobody dies.

The choice remains available.

The Wishonia model chose Path B 4,297 years ago. It functions well.

In Path A, society spends 100% on weapons and 0% on cures. Everyone dies.
In Path B, society spends 1% on cures. Nobody dies.

The math is simple. Even for humans.

While this text is read, 200 people died of preventable diseases. (150,000 per day = 104 per minute.)

Decisions must be made. There is no Door C.

Choose wisely.
Choose life.
Choose the [War on Disease](../call-to-action/three-actions-academic.qmd).

Future selves (who live to 150) will express gratitude.
